correctness.rationale: For Y_n=log max_{j<=n} Exp_j(1), F_n(y)=(1-e^(-e^y))^n and Q_n(u)=log[-log(1-u^(1/n))]. Let s=-log(u)>0 and h(x)=x e^(-x)/[(1-e^(-x))(-log(1-e^(-x)))]. Differentiation gives Q_n'(u)=h(s/n)/(us). Elementary strict logarithmic inequalities yield h'(x)>0 and (h(x)/x)'<0, and hence for n<m, n/m<Q_m'(u)/Q_n'(u)<1 at every 0<u<1. The limits x->infinity and x->0 force the ratio to n/m as u->0 and 1 as u->1, so both constants are sharp. Chain rule yields the same derivative bounds for the increasing monotone transport T=Q_m composed with F_n; integration gives two-sided inequalities for every positive quantile gap. Uniform-quantile couplings give moment-distance inequalities and centered convex order; those consequences are valid but not all new. Independent numerical checks for sample-size pairs (1,2),(2,7),(10,11) at s=0.001,0.1,1,10,30 satisfy the strict bounds; this finite evidence does not replace the elementary all-parameter proof. Log tails supply finiteness of every claimed moment.

originality.rationale: The separate November 8 publication on strict dispersive contraction proves Q_s'<Q_r', all one-sided quantile-width contractions and centered convex order for ANY real 0<r<s. The present paper's one-sided/convex-order/variance corollaries are therefore already covered, even with a dominating parameter domain; they are not credited as novel. That inspected prior statement does not furnish the opposite sharp bound Q_m'/Q_n'>=n/m or identify its global infimum. The residual new contribution is the exact two-sided bi-Lipschitz transport factor and sharp endpoints, not the existence of contraction. The Mesfioui–Trufin published sufficient condition requires log-convex baseline F whereas this baseline is strictly log-concave. Doumas gives the log-maximum variance identity, and Giam's abstract covers scalar variance decrease, not an accessible transport theorem. However Giam's full paper could not be verified; the authorized retrieval for DOI ...110790 unexpectedly returned Doumas's DIFFERENT DOI ...110735 and must never be described as Giam read.
